the_argument.per_scale_bound: lintegral_hausdorffMeasure_stratum_le: run Mathlib's approximating partition on u ITSELF so one partition serves both components; on each piece the local package makes the projected map c-epsilon-Lipschitz along every fibre of the regular component; the Eilenberg bound applies INSIDE A FIBRE at exponent k with a target of dimension m - r, where k + (m - r) = n - r is exactly right; integrating over the fibre parameter against the PROVED regular coarea formula with weight 1 turns the fibre measures into an ordinary integral of the coarea Jacobian; the target-splitting identity reads the result as an integral over the target. THE CONSTANT DOES NOT DEPEND ON EPSILON.
the_argument.limit: exists_nhds_ae_hausdorffMeasure_stratum_inter_levelSet_eq_zero: the right-hand factor is finite because the neighbourhood's closure is compact and the coarea Jacobian is continuous, and the exponent m - r is positive exactly because r < m, so the integral over the target vanishes and the integrand vanishes almost everywhere
the_argument.where_the_exponent_is_repaired: the fibre. Applying the same Eilenberg bound in the ambient space forces the exponent k + r; forcing it back to k puts mu_H[n-r] of a set of positive Lebesgue measure on the right, which is infinity - exactly the obstruction N2 records. Inside a fibre the bound is used at k and the right-hand side is the fibre's own finite H^(n-r) measure.
the_argument.engines_used: the same two the R5 and R6 rounds established - the proved regular coarea formula and measure-preserving change of variables with Tonelli - in their INTEGRAL rather than null-set form

what_R7_is_not: it is a statement about ONE stratum in ONE neighbourhood
it says nothing about the whole critical set, which is the union of the strata of every rank r < m and needs R8 to assemble
it is not a coarea formula in a new case and does not extend the applicability of the proved one
it is not a Sard theorem: nothing is claimed about the measure of the set of critical values
